cases.title: Wildfire in Negev shrubland under a khamsin
cases.plain_english: Satellite picks up a fire in the Lahav shrubland of the northern Negev on a 41 C August afternoon, with a dry 50 km/h east wind. Lahav, Lehavim and Dvir lie to the west of it.

expected.note: Continuous shrubland, dry, windy — this must run and reach the downwind towns while leaving the upwind one alone.

planner_json.event_description: Wildfire incident at open ground, spreading west at 70.61 metres per minute through shrubland. Spread severity critical (100 of 100) over the next 180.0 minutes. Evacuation preparation for Lehavim, Rahat. 42,963 residents inside the forecast fire perimeter. 79,041 residents in settlements on the forecast path. Hazardous sites in the path: concrete plant. Exclusion and hazardous-material considerations apply. Sites whose occupants cannot self-evacuate in the path: hospital. Assisted evacuation and transport required. Requires decisions on unit types to commit, evacuation, road closures, structure protection and crew safety at the fireline.
limitations: Unsuppressed spread: no crew, engine, aircraft or existing containment is modelled.
Surface fire only: spotting ahead of the front and sustained crown runs are not modelled.
Barriers finer than the land-cover grid — a road, a firebreak, a wadi — are invisible here.
Arrival times assume the forecast wind holds for the whole horizon.

cases.title: Judean hills, light wind on steep ground

expected.note: Slope is 17 degrees mean, 35 degrees steepest. With a 5 km/h breeze the slope term should dominate the heading.

cases.title: Detection on the Dead Sea shore, no surface data
cases.plain_english: A hotspot on the Dead Sea shore, where the land-cover grid has a genuine hole — the survey maps no vegetation there at all.

expected.note: Must degrade honestly: no score, no zero, and a report that says the absence is about the data and not about the fire.

planner_json.why: The analysis made no forecast, so there is nothing to plan from. Planning anyway would fabricate a basis for dispatch.

cases.title: Upper Galilee woodland in January rain
cases.plain_english: The same kind of fuel as the Carmel case, in the wet season: 9 C, 95% humidity, saturated fuel. Nothing should carry.

expected.note: Must stall for wetness, named differently from the no-data case. 'Nothing to burn' and 'too wet to burn' are different facts and are acted on differently.
